action: Initiate scanning of the liver using an intercostal approach.
interpretation: Change the scanning window to view the liver through the rib spaces.

action: Assess the superficial liver parenchyma via the intercostal window.
interpretation: Observe that liver anatomy previously located in the far field (during subcostal scanning) is now visualized in the near field.

action: Slide the probe superiorly and inferiorly, moving up and down between the rib spaces.
interpretation: Utilize this different angle to visualize the actual liver parenchyma, avoiding rib shadows.

action: Continue sliding the probe up and down through various rib spaces until the kidney is visualized.
interpretation: Identify the right kidney as it comes into view during the intercostal sweep.

action: Focus on the right kidney structure.
interpretation: Confirm that the kidney appears grossly normal.

action: Compare the echogenicity of the renal cortex to the adjacent liver parenchyma.
interpretation: Assess the hepato-renal interface. Verify that the kidney is slightly darker (hypoechoic) or isoechoic ('just the same') relative to the liver.

action: Rotate the probe to a transverse orientation while intercostal. Subsequently, transition to scanning the right kidney in the supine position.
interpretation: Inspect the liver in transverse to detect potential masses missed in other views. Re-evaluate the right kidney in the supine position to confirm it remains grossly normal.
